thesis.name: Portable and FAIR Query Functions with WebAssembly and SPARQL
thesis.description: Created a pipeline enabling SPARQL queries to execute User-Defined Functions (UDFs), executing UDFs using isolated WebAssembly environments, semantically defining UDFs using the Function Ontology, and making UDFs more accessible and reusable following FAIR principles.
candidate_bullets: Implemented a pipeline enabling SPARQL queries to execute User-Defined Functions (UDFs) in isolated WebAssembly environments.
Executed UDFs through WebAssembly isolation to provide a controlled execution environment for SPARQL query functions.
Described UDFs using the Function Ontology to support their accessibility, discoverability, and reuse.
Applied FAIR principles to the design and semantic description of reusable SPARQL query functions.
Compared execution times between WebAssembly-based UDFs and equivalent native functions.
general_bullets: Implemented a pipeline enabling SPARQL queries to execute User-Defined Functions (UDFs) in isolated WebAssembly environments.
Described UDFs using the Function Ontology to support their accessibility, discoverability, and reuse.
Compared execution times between WebAssembly-based UDFs and equivalent native functions.

projects.name: Customer Churn Prediction Project
candidate_bullets: Developed an end-to-end customer churn prediction pipeline using pandas and scikit-learn, covering data auditing, cleaning, EDA, preprocessing, and classification.
Built Logistic Regression and Random Forest models using scikit-learn pipelines with numerical scaling and categorical one-hot encoding.
Evaluated model performance using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrices.
Tuned the Logistic Regression classification threshold to examine precision-recall trade-offs and identify operating points suited to different retention priorities.
Interpreted Logistic Regression coefficients alongside exploratory analysis to identify relationships between churn and factors including tenure, contract type, and internet service.
Compared baseline models and documented findings, limitations, and potential improvements in a structured GitHub project.

projects.name: House Pricing Prediction
candidate_bullets: Developed an end-to-end house price prediction pipeline using pandas and scikit-learn, covering data auditing, EDA, feature analysis, preprocessing, and regression modeling.
Built Ridge Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting models using scikit-learn pipelines with numerical preprocessing, categorical encoding, and custom missing-value handling.
Evaluated models using MAE, RMSE, and MAPE, comparing performance across increasingly complex regression approaches.
Performed residual and error analysis to investigate prediction errors, identify unusual properties, and assess potential systematic prediction bias.
Selected Gradient Boosting after reducing MAE from approximately $21.4K with the Ridge baseline to $14.1K on the test set.
Documented the complete modeling workflow, findings, limitations, and potential improvements in a structured GitHub project using four focused notebooks.
general_bullets: Developed an end-to-end house price prediction pipeline using pandas and scikit-learn, covering data auditing, EDA, feature analysis, preprocessing, and regression modeling.

projects.name: Movie Score Prediction
candidate_bullets: Developed a movie score prediction pipeline using pandas and scikit-learn, including data cleaning, feature selection, preprocessing, and regression modeling.
Built a custom scikit-learn transformer to convert multi-label genre data into binary features for model training.
Implemented reusable preprocessing pipelines with ColumnTransformer, handling numerical imputation, categorical encoding, and multi-label genre transformation.
Compared Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost regression models using 5-fold cross-validation and Mean Absolute Error.
Prepared a cleaned movie dataset by selecting relevant features and handling missing values in categorical and production-related attributes.
